# R1.11 -- Derivation of the 100,568 potentially avoidable presentations, and single- vs multi-algorithm comparison

*Supplementary analysis for the IJPDS revision. Generated by `r1_11_r1_13_single_vs_multiple.R` from `ANALYSIS/ed_single.parquet` (the published analysis sample: one first ED presentation per patient, N = 201,106). Every number below is produced by that script.*

## Verdict

The 100,568 figure is a **union, not a sum**. Every presentation was assigned to exactly one of eight mutually exclusive cells defined by `paste0(nyu, res, acuity_out)`; the seven cells in which at least one algorithm fires add to 100,568 (50.0% of the 201,106 presentations), and the eighth cell, "000", holds the 100,538 presentations no algorithm flags. Adding the three algorithm totals instead (68,173 Diagnosis + 48,181 Resources + 15,716 Triage-Acuity = 132,070) would overstate the burden by 31,502, because 25,162 presentations are flagged by exactly two algorithms and 3,170 by all three.

A combined estimate is reported because the three algorithms operationalise different and only partly overlapping constructs of avoidability -- retrospective discharge diagnosis, resources actually consumed, and triage-assigned acuity -- so their union answers the policy question "how many presentations would *any* accepted method regard as potentially avoidable" without counting a presentation twice, while the seven-cell breakdown below allows any single-algorithm estimate to be recovered exactly.

On the reviewer's second question, **the two largest apparent differences are definitional and must not be read as empirical findings.** Triage acuity and admission are *inputs* to two of the three algorithms, and MULTIPLE carries those flags far more often than SINGLE (Triage-Acuity flag 38.9% vs 6.5%; Resources flag 87.4% vs 32.4%). `acuity_out` is an exact recode of the triage score (`acuity_out == (acuity >= 4)` for all 201,106 rows), and the Resources flag forces disposition never to be ADMITTED. So the raw acuity gap (3.28 vs 2.76) and the raw admission gap (0.2% vs 14.0%) are largely arithmetic: restricting to presentations that do not carry the Triage-Acuity flag shrinks the acuity gap from 0.52 to 0.13 points (SMD -0.792 to -0.264), and admission cannot be cleanly compared at all, because the only multi-algorithm presentations without the Resources flag are the 3,578 in group "101", which carry the Triage-Acuity flag and are therefore rarely admitted for that second, equally definitional reason.

What does survive is narrower but genuine. **ED length of stay** is robust: multi-algorithm presentations are shorter by any cut -- raw 363.1 vs 227.2 minutes (SMD +0.577), and still 352.0 vs 226.9 minutes among non-admitted presentations only (SMD +0.528), so the gap is not an artefact of the admission constraint. **Comorbidity is much weaker than it first appears**: the raw Charlson gap (0.23 vs 0.07; SMD +0.341) falls to 0.10 vs 0.07 (SMD +0.121) once admitted presentations are excluded, because comorbidity capture is itself driven by admission (mean Charlson 1.22 in admitted vs 0.11 in discharged-home presentations, reflecting roughly five times as much diagnosis coding). **ICD chapter differences are also confounded**, because the primary discharge diagnosis is the input to the Diagnosis algorithm and 84.9% of MULTIPLE carries that flag versus 61.1% of SINGLE.

Demographic differences remain small and are unaffected by any of this, since age, sex, race and pain are not inputs to any algorithm: multi-algorithm presentations are modestly younger (mean 41.5 vs 44.9 years; SMD +0.179) and modestly less often recorded as White (51.7% vs 58.8%; SMD +0.142), while sex is essentially identical (56.9% vs 56.7% female; SMD -0.003) and the remaining race/ethnicity categories (|SMD| <= 0.090) and recorded pain score (SMD +0.091) fall below the threshold.

**Revised interpretation.** A severity-gradient reading is still defensible, but it now rests on ED length of stay, on the presenting-complaint distribution (R1.13), and on the demographic null -- not on acuity or admission, which are restatements of the algorithms' own definitions. It should also be stated as a limitation that **no fully clean contrast is available**: the stratum with neither the Resources nor the Triage-Acuity flag contains **no** multi-algorithm presentations (it can only contain Diagnosis-only presentations, which are single by definition), so acuity and disposition can never be compared free of both constraints. Readers should treat "presentations flagged by more algorithms are less acute and less often admitted" as true by construction, and rely on length of stay and presenting complaint for the substantive claim.

> **A note on inference.** With 72,236 versus 28,332 presentations, conventional significance tests return p < 0.001 for essentially every variable examined, including differences of a fraction of a year of age that carry no clinical or policy meaning. P-values are therefore not reported. All comparisons use standardised mean differences (SMD): continuous variables as `(m1 - m2) / sqrt((sd1^2 + sd2^2)/2)`, categorical variables per category as `(p1 - p2) / sqrt((p1(1-p1) + p2(1-p2))/2)`, with the conventional |SMD| > 0.1 threshold marking a non-negligible difference.

## Part 1 -- How the 100,568 was derived

### 1a. The eight mutually exclusive overlap groups

Each presentation falls in exactly one cell of `combined_group = paste0(nyu, res, acuity_out)`. The seven non-zero cells partition the flagged set and add to 100,568 with no double-counting.

| Overlap group (nyu/res/acuity) | Algorithms flagging the visit | No. of algorithms | N visits | % of 100,568 flagged | % of 201,106 sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | Diagnosis only | 1 | 44,119 | 43.9 | 21.9 |
| 010 | Resources only | 1 | 23,427 | 23.3 | 11.6 |
| 001 | Triage-Acuity only | 1 | 4,690 | 4.7 | 2.3 |
| 110 | Diagnosis + Resources | 2 | 17,306 | 17.2 | 8.6 |
| 101 | Diagnosis + Triage-Acuity | 2 | 3,578 | 3.6 | 1.8 |
| 011 | Resources + Triage-Acuity | 2 | 4,278 | 4.3 | 2.1 |
| 111 | All three | 3 | 3,170 | 3.2 | 1.6 |
| SINGLE subtotal | exactly one algorithm | 1 | 72,236 | 71.8 | 35.9 |
| MULTIPLE subtotal | two or three algorithms | 2-3 | 28,332 | 28.2 | 14.1 |
| **TOTAL FLAGGED** | any algorithm | >=1 | **100,568** | 100.0 | 50.0 |
| 000 | Not flagged (reference) | 0 | 100,538 | - | 50.0 |

### 1b. Relationship to the three (overlapping) algorithm totals

| Step | N | % of 201,106 |
|---|---|---|
| Diagnosis algorithm (NYU-based) flags | 68,173 | 33.9 |
| Resources algorithm flags | 48,181 | 24.0 |
| Triage-Acuity algorithm flags | 15,716 | 7.8 |
| Arithmetic sum of the three algorithm totals | 132,070 | 65.7 |
| less visits counted more than once (double-counting) | -31,502 | - |
| **Union: visits flagged by >=1 algorithm** | **100,568** | **50.0** |

### 1c. Where the 31,502 excess comes from

A presentation flagged by exactly two algorithms is counted once too often in the arithmetic sum; one flagged by all three is counted twice too often.

| Source | Visits | Excess counts |
|---|---|---|
| Visits flagged by exactly 2 algorithms (counted 1 extra time each) | 25,162 | 25,162 |
| Visits flagged by all 3 algorithms (counted 2 extra times each) | 3,170 | 6,340 |
| **Total double-counting** | 28,332 | **31,502** |

Arithmetic check: (25,162 x 1) + (3,170 x 2) = 31,502 = 132,070 - 100,568.

### 1d. How much of each algorithm's yield is unique

This is the substantive rationale for reporting a combined estimate: no algorithm is a subset of another, and each contributes a large block of presentations that no other algorithm identifies. Reporting only one algorithm, or reporting the three totals without their union, would therefore either understate the burden or overstate it by 31,502.

| Algorithm | Total flagged | Flagged by this algorithm alone | % of its yield that is unique | Shared with >=1 other algorithm | % of its yield that is shared |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Diagnosis (NYU-based) | 68,173 | 44,119 | 64.7 | 24,054 | 35.3 |
| Resources | 48,181 | 23,427 | 48.6 | 24,754 | 51.4 |
| Triage-Acuity | 15,716 | 4,690 | 29.8 | 11,026 | 70.2 |

## Part 2B -- Definitional-constraint audit

This section exists because several variables in Part 2 are **inputs to the algorithms themselves**. Group membership therefore partly determines them, and the raw contrast overstates the empirical difference. (This is the same issue Reviewer 2 raises at R2.2.)

### 2B.1 How often each group carries each algorithm flag

This is the mechanism: MULTIPLE carries the constraining flags far more often, so any variable those flags constrain will differ between the groups whether or not anything clinically distinct is happening.

| Group | N | Carries Diagnosis flag | Carries Resources flag | Carries Triage-Acuity flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SINGLE | 72,236 | 61.1% | 32.4% | 6.5% |
| MULTIPLE | 28,332 | 84.9% | 87.4% | 38.9% |
| UNFLAGGED | 100,538 | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |

### 2B.2 What each flag forces

Each row was verified against the data; all violating-row counts are zero (see the verification table above).

| Algorithm flag | What it forces about the visit | Variable in Part 2 affected |
|---|---|---|
| Triage-Acuity (`acuity_out`) | `acuity_out` is an exact recode of the triage score: `acuity_out == (acuity >= 4)` for all 201,106 rows | `acuity` -- **fully determined** |
| Resources (`res`) | disposition is never ADMITTED (and never TRANSFER or EXPIRED) | `disposition` (ADMITTED) -- **fully determined** |
| Resources (`res`) | disposition is never ADMITTED, so the only remaining ways to end a visit early are eloped / left without being seen / against advice | `disposition` (left before completing care) -- *inflated* |
| Resources (`res`) | no ECG rhythm is ever recorded and no medication is ever dispensed in the ED -- both markers of longer, more intensive care | `length_of_stay` (indirectly), `cci_score` (via admission) |
| Diagnosis (`nyu`) | classification is computed FROM the primary discharge diagnosis, so ICD chapter is an input | `icd_chapter` |

### 2B.3 Raw versus constraint-removed comparisons

For each affected variable, the raw contrast is shown against the contrast computed after removing the presentations whose values the flag forces.

| Variable | Stratum | SINGLE n | SINGLE value | MULTIPLE n | MULTIPLE value | SMD | abs(SMD)>0.1 |

| Triage acuity (mean) | Without Triage-Acuity flag | 67,546 | 2.67 | 17,306 | 2.80 | -0.264 | **yes** |

| Admitted (%) | Without Resources flag | 48,809 | 20.8% | 3,578 | 1.5% | +0.644 | **yes** |
| Left before completing care (%) | Raw -- *partly definitional* | 72,236 | 2.8% | 28,332 | 9.5% | -0.283 | **yes** |
| Left before completing care (%) | Without Resources flag | 48,809 | 1.0% | 3,578 | 1.4% | -0.032 | no |
| ED length of stay (min) | Raw | 72,236 | 363.09 | 28,332 | 227.20 | +0.577 | **yes** |
| ED length of stay (min) | Without Resources flag | 48,804 | 394.99 | 3,578 | 212.94 | +0.709 | **yes** |
| ED length of stay (min) | Non-admitted only | 62,089 | 352.04 | 28,256 | 226.89 | +0.528 | **yes** |
| ED length of stay (min) | Non-admitted AND without Resources flag | 38,673 | 385.61 | 3,525 | 210.23 | +0.668 | **yes** |

| Charlson comorbidity (mean) | Non-admitted only | 62,105 | 0.10 | 28,279 | 0.07 | +0.121 | **yes** |

Reading this table:

- **Triage acuity is largely definitional.** The raw gap of 0.52 points (SMD -0.792) falls to 0.13 points (SMD -0.264) once presentations carrying the Triage-Acuity flag are excluded -- roughly three-quarters of the raw gap is arithmetic. A real residual difference remains, but it is small.
- **Admission cannot be cleanly compared.** The raw 14.0% vs 0.2% is close to arithmetic necessity, since 87.4% of MULTIPLE carries the Resources flag and that flag forbids admission. Restricting to presentations without the flag does not fix this: the SMD actually rises (+0.559 to +0.644) because the only remaining multi-algorithm presentations are the 3,578 in group "101", which all carry the Triage-Acuity flag and are therefore rarely admitted for a second definitional reason. **Neither figure should be presented as an empirical contrast.**
- **Leaving before completing care is partly definitional too.** Presentations carrying the Resources flag account for almost all such episodes (the flag permits eloped / left-without-being-seen but forbids admission), and the contrast weakens from SMD -0.283 to -0.032 once those presentations are removed.
- **Length of stay survives.** It does not attenuate under any restriction: SMD +0.577 raw, +0.709 excluding the Resources flag, +0.528 among non-admitted presentations only, and +0.668 under both restrictions. This is the strongest non-definitional clinical difference in the analysis.
- **Comorbidity largely does not survive.** The raw Charlson SMD of +0.341 falls to +0.121 among non-admitted presentations. Most of the apparent comorbidity difference is an artefact of differential admission, which is itself definitionally constrained (see 2B.5).

### 2B.4 No fully clean contrast exists

The stratum carrying neither the Resources nor the Triage-Acuity flag contains **no multi-algorithm presentations**. This is a structural consequence of the design rather than a feature of these data: a presentation with neither flag can only be flagged by the Diagnosis algorithm, and a presentation flagged by the Diagnosis algorithm alone is single-algorithm by definition. Acuity and disposition therefore can never be compared between SINGLE and MULTIPLE free of both constraints, and this should be stated as a limitation.

| Group | Overlap group | N |
|---|---|---|
| SINGLE | 100 | 44,119 |
| UNFLAGGED | 000 | 100,538 |

### 2B.5 Why the comorbidity difference is mostly an admission artefact

Charlson score is computed from recorded ICD codes, and admitted presentations carry several times more coded diagnoses than discharged ones. Because the Resources flag forbids admission, and 87.4% of MULTIPLE carries that flag, the comorbidity gap is substantially downstream of a definitional constraint rather than an independent clinical finding.

| Disposition | N | Mean Charlson | Mean length of ICD code string |
|---|---|---|---|
| HOME | 121,407 | 0.11 | 14.3 |
| ADMITTED | 68,847 | 1.22 | 77.0 |
| TRANSFER | 3,141 | 0.20 | 27.8 |
| LEFT WITHOUT BEING SEEN | 2,597 | 0.02 | 6.4 |
| OTHER | 2,344 | 0.53 | 39.9 |
| ELOPED | 1,913 | 0.08 | 12.2 |
| LEFT AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE | 756 | 0.23 | 16.9 |
| EXPIRED | 101 | 0.34 | 13.9 |

### 2B.6 ICD chapter is an input to the Diagnosis algorithm

The Diagnosis (NYU-based) algorithm classifies presentations *from* the primary discharge diagnosis, so ICD chapter is an algorithm input, and the flag is carried by 84.9% of MULTIPLE versus 61.1% of SINGLE. Restricting to presentations without the Diagnosis flag leaves a multi-algorithm stratum consisting only of group "011" (n = 4,278), whose chapter profile is completely unlike the raw comparison -- confirming that the raw ICD chapter contrast is confounded by differential Diagnosis-flag prevalence and should not be presented as a clean empirical difference.

| Group | ICD chapter | N | % |
|---|---|---|---|
| SINGLE | Injury and poisoning | 11,262 | 40.1 |
| SINGLE | Ill-defined conditions | 6,510 | 23.2 |
| SINGLE | Mental disorders | 4,199 | 14.9 |
| MULTIPLE | Injury and poisoning | 3,436 | 80.3 |
| MULTIPLE | Mental disorders | 163 | 3.8 |
| MULTIPLE | Factors influencing health status/contact with health services | 138 | 3.2 |

### 2B.7 Presenting complaint is not an algorithm input

None of the three algorithms uses the free-text chief complaint: the Diagnosis algorithm uses the primary discharge diagnosis, the Resources algorithm uses rhythm documentation, ED medication dispensing and disposition, and the Triage-Acuity algorithm uses the ESI score. The complaint-cluster analysis reported in `r1_13_single_vs_multiple_complaints.md` is therefore the least contaminated evidence available, and its cluster-level SMDs are almost unchanged when the admission channel is removed (see Part 3e of that file).

---

## Notes on interpretation

- **The `Algorithm input?` column marks how far each row is forced by construction.** `**DEFINITIONAL**` means the algorithms' own definitions determine the value; `*partly definitional*` means a substantial share of the difference is forced; `residual` and `sensitivity` rows are the constraint-removed re-computations; `no` means the variable is not used by any algorithm.
- **Triage acuity is scored 1 (most acute) to 5 (least acute)**, so the higher mean in the MULTIPLE column denotes *lower* clinical acuity.
- **`prior_visits_1yr` and `revisit_72hrs` are near-constant in this sample by construction.** The published analysis sample retains one *first* ED presentation per patient, so almost no presentation has a prior visit in the preceding year and almost none is followed by a recorded 72-hour revisit. They are reported for completeness but carry essentially no information about the single-versus-multiple contrast in this sample.
- **ED length of stay is expressed in minutes.**
- Race/ethnicity is collapsed from the raw MIMIC-IV strings using `str_detect`, testing Hispanic/Latino first so that entries such as `HISPANIC/LATINO - PUERTO RICAN` are not absorbed into White. `UNKNOWN`, `PATIENT DECLINED TO ANSWER`, `PORTUGUESE`, `SOUTH AMERICAN`, `AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE`, `NATIVE HAWAIIAN OR OTHER PACIFIC ISLANDER`, `MULTIPLE RACE/ETHNICITY` and `UNABLE TO OBTAIN` fall into Other.
- Pain score is missing for a small number of presentations; missing counts are given in the table and those presentations are excluded from the pain statistics only.

See `r1_13_single_vs_multiple_complaints.md` for the corresponding presenting-complaint analysis (R1.13).

## Note on the medication field (added during review of this file)

The Resources algorithm's medication criterion is `is.na(pre_gsn_count)`. That column is
built from `mimic-iv-ed-2.2/ed/pyxis.csv.gz`, which records medications dispensed from the
Pyxis cabinet **during the ED stay**. It is not a discharge prescription.

The separate column `med_gsn_count` is built from `medrecon.csv.gz`, the medication
reconciliation list — the medicines the patient was already taking before arrival. That
column is not used by any of the three algorithms.

Earlier wording in this file described the criterion as a discharge prescription. The
computation always used `pre_gsn_count` and is unaffected; only the description was wrong
and has been corrected. The correct reading of the Resources criterion is "no medication
was dispensed to the patient in the ED".
